title: Prices on a minimum-spend floor
heading: Subgradient Steps Raise the Price of an Overspent Year and Lower the Price of an Underspent One
cases: when the bound equals the best plan's value, the step is zero and the prices do not move
a year whose relaxed plan spends less than its floor gets a higher price, and one above it a lower price
a price that the step would push below zero stops at zero
the step length divides the bound's excess by the sum of the squared subgradient entries
a relaxed plan that spends every floor exactly has a zero subgradient, and the prices stay as they are
